answer: Protocol security rests on significant collateralized staking and quadratic slashing, ensuring capital erosion for malicious acts scales quadratically. This guarantees super-linear marginal attack costs; any Sybil cluster incurs exponentially increasing capital expenditure, consistently making extracted value far less than attack costs. Such negative expected utility creates a robust Nash equilibrium, deterring even a formidable knoll of adversaries from siphoning protocol nectar or reaching the system's security summit, thus sustaining robust consensus.
